breakthroughAssessment.justification: The paper presents a rigorous theoretical framework unifying online A/B-testing with Off-Policy Evaluation, demonstrating strong variance reduction benefits by exploiting policy overlap. The analytical proofs, novel estimators (Delta-MRDR, Delta-DCG with optimal baselines), and optimal traffic allocation insights are significant contributions to the field of online experimentation and causal inference. While empirical validation is primarily simulation-based, the results are compelling and point to practical utility for large-scale online platforms, enabling more efficient and robust A/B tests.

coreProblem.concreteExample: When a treatment and control policy in an A/B-test agree on an action, the observed outcome contributes noise but no signal regarding the treatment effect, unnecessarily inflating confidence intervals.
coreProblem.statement: Online controlled experiments (A/B-tests) are expensive and suffer from high variance, which limits statistical power in assessing treatment effects. Standard variance reduction techniques leverage model-based control variates but often remain agnostic to potential structural relationships between competing policies.
whyItMatters: High variance inhibits practitioners from attaining tight confidence intervals around Average Treatment Effects (ATEs), limiting statistical power.
Detecting small incremental model updates requires prolonged test durations or substantial traffic allocation, both of which impose material opportunity costs.
Policy overlap, where treatment and control policies often agree on actions, is common in practice but its statistical implications for variance reduction are rarely exploited.

evaluationHighlights: The policy-aware Delta-IPS estimator strictly dominates the standard Difference-in-Means (DiM) estimator in terms of Mean Squared Error (MSE) on Average Treatment Effects (ATE), demonstrating robustness across varying action space sizes and reducing MSE significantly in high-overlap regimes.
Optimal treatment allocation, deviating from a balanced 50/50 split, can yield an approximately 18% variance reduction compared to standard practice in asymmetric policy settings.

The Delta-MRDR objective significantly reduces ATE estimation variance by 75% compared to Delta-Beta-IPS and 8% compared to Delta-DR in heterogeneous environments, by focusing model capacity on regions of policy disagreement.

The Delta-Beta-perp-perp-DCG estimator effectively combats variance explosion in top-K ranking evaluation at high policy divergence, maintaining strict variance advantage over DiM and unbaselined Delta-DCG across the entire divergence spectrum.

experimentFigures.caption: Mean Squared Error (MSE) of the standard DiM estimator and the Policy-Aware $\Delta$-IPS estimator for varying action space sizes $|A|$. The $x$-axis represents policy divergence (proxied by the inverse temperature $\frac{1}{T}$ of $\pi'$). We observe that the $\Delta$-OPE view successfully exploits policy overlap to significantly reduce estimation error, remaining robust across large action spaces.

Visualising optimal treatment allocation ($p^{\star}$) in an asymmetric policy setting. We compare a conservative control policy $\pi'$ against an exploratory treatment policy $\pi$. We validate that empirical estimation variance tracks the theoretical variance proxy $J(p)$ derived in Eq. 23 up to a multiplicative constant. The minimum variance is achieved at $p^{\star} \approx 0.81$, reducing variance by 18% compared to an even split.

Variance reduction via the $\Delta$-MRDR objective in a highly heterogeneous environment. The $\Delta\beta^{\star}$-IPS estimator serves as the optimal model-free baseline. The $\Delta$-DR estimator minimises global MSE, causing it to overfit to the noisy majority and mischaracterise the baseline for the target group, resulting in suboptimal variance. The $\Delta$-MRDR estimator targets model capacity exclusively at the regions of high policy divergence, learning the correct local relationship and significantly reducing ATE estimation variance.

Empirical variance of top-$K$ ranking estimators across varying levels of policy divergence ($1-\alpha$), shown on a logarithmic scale. The standard A/B testing procedure (DiM) suffers from high variance regardless of policy overlap. The unbaselined $\Delta$-DCG estimator performs well under high overlap but suffers from severe variance explosion as divergence increases. The $\Delta\beta^{\star}_{\perp\perp}$-DCG estimator utilises position-specific optimal baselines to mitigate this explosion, achieving significant variance reduction compared to the standard A/B test across all divergence regimes.

mainTakeaways: The proposed policy-aware $\Delta$-OPE estimators ($\Delta$-IPS, $\Delta$-DR) strictly dominate the standard Difference-in-Means (DiM) estimator, especially when policies exhibit common support (overlap).
Optimal treatment allocation can significantly deviate from the traditional 50/50 split, favoring exploratory policies to minimize estimation variance and maximize statistical power.
The $\Delta$-MRDR objective effectively reduces ATE estimation variance by concentrating model capacity on regions of policy disagreement.
The framework extends to combinatorial ranking action spaces via $\Delta$-DCG, which, when combined with position-specific optimal baselines, combats variance explosion at high policy divergence.

explanation: A formal proof demonstrating that the resulting policy-aware estimators strictly dominate the standard DiM estimator in terms of variance, given common support and non-zero residual variance.

Derivation of a variance-optimal traffic allocation ratio ($p^{\star}$) that can deviate from a balanced 50/50 split, determined by policy divergence and the curvature of variance, offering guidance for experimental design.

Introduction of the $\Delta$-MRDR (More Robust Doubly Robust) objective, which trains reward models to explicitly minimize ATE estimation variance by focusing learning on regions of policy disagreement.

Extension of the framework to combinatorial ranking applications with the $\Delta$-DCG estimator and position-specific optimal baselines ($\Delta\beta^{\star}_{\perp\perp}$-DCG) to combat variance explosion inherent in off-policy ranking evaluation.
keyNovelty.main: Applying the $\Delta$-Off-Policy Estimation ($\Delta$-OPE) framework to online A/B-testing by interpreting treatment assignment as a meta-policy, which leverages policy overlap to accelerate experimentation and reduce variance.

keyTerms.definition: The causal effect of a treatment, typically estimated as the difference in expected outcomes between a treatment group and a control group.
The task of evaluating the performance of a new policy using data collected from a different logging (behavior) policy.
A technique used in off-policy evaluation to re-weight logged data from a behavior policy to estimate the performance of a target policy.
An estimator that combines importance sampling with a model-based control variate, providing unbiased estimates if either the importance weights or the reward model are correctly specified.

The degree to which two policies (treatment and control) agree on the actions they would recommend for a given context; specifically, the region where both policies assign positive probability to an action.

comparisonToPriorWork: Standard variance reduction techniques in A/B-testing are typically agnostic to structural relationships between policies, whereas this work explicitly leverages policy overlap.

The paper formally establishes exact equivalences between online DiM and $\Delta\beta^{\star}$-IPS, and between RADiM and $\Delta$-DR, bridging online controlled experiments and off-policy evaluation frameworks.

Unlike prior work (e.g., Konishi et al. [43], Sakhi et al. [60]) that bounds reward variance or uses variance surrogates, this work provides exact variance dominance proofs and derives an analytical variance-optimal traffic allocation.
This work extends the framework to combinatorial ranking spaces with the $\Delta$-DCG estimator, which previous comparable methods did not explicitly address.
limitations: Empirical validation is based solely on synthetic simulation environments, which, despite offering ground-truth counterfactuals, necessarily simplify reward structure, context distributions, and policy behavior, making real-world uplift predictions less certain.

The proposed estimators require knowledge of exact policy probabilities $\pi(a|x)$ and $\pi'(a|x)$, which can be computationally expensive or numerically unstable in large action spaces or sequence generation settings (e.g., for LLMs).

The variance-optimal traffic allocation $p^{\star}$ derivation assumes stationarity of the context distribution and homoskedasticity of outcomes for the analytical solution under $\Delta$-IPS, though an adaptive two-stage design is suggested to mitigate the latter.
The robustness of $p^{\star}$ to distribution shifts (common in live recommender systems) remains an open question, requiring future work on fully sequential adaptive designs.

modeling.label: Policy Mixture for Meta-Policy
modeling.value: The randomized treatment assignment in A/B-testing is reframed as a meta-policy $\pi_0(a|x) = p\pi(a|x) + (1-p)\pi'(a|x)$, where $p$ is the treatment allocation ratio.

modeling.label: Delta-IPS Estimator
modeling.value: An unbiased estimator for ATE: $\hat{\text{V}}_{\Delta \text{-IPS}} = \frac{1}{|D|} \sum_{(x,a,y) \in D} \frac{\Delta(a|x)}{\pi_0(a|x)} y$, where $\Delta(a|x) = \pi(a|x) - \pi'(a|x)$.

modeling.label: Delta-Doubly Robust (DR) Estimator
modeling.value: A variance-reduced estimator that leverages a learned reward model $f(x,a)$: $\hat{\text{V}}_{\Delta \text{-DR}} = \frac{1}{|D|} \sum_{(x,a,y) \in D} \left( \hat{\tau}(x) + \frac{\Delta(a|x)}{\pi_0(a|x)} (y - f(x,a)) \right)$, with $\hat{\tau}(x) = \sum_{a \in \text{A}} \Delta(a|x) f(x,a)$.

modeling.label: Delta-MRDR Objective
modeling.value: A Weighted Least Squares objective for learning reward models ($f_\theta$) that minimize ATE estimation variance by focusing on regions of policy disagreement: $\theta^{\star} = \text{arg min}_{\theta} \text{E}_{(x,a,y) \sim D} \left[ \left( \frac{\Delta(a|x)}{\pi_0(a|x)} (y - f_\theta(x,a)) \right)^2 \right]$.

modeling.label: Delta-DCG Estimator
modeling.value: An estimator for ATE in ranking, replacing action propensities with exposure propensities: $\hat{\text{V}}_{\Delta \text{-DCG}} = \frac{1}{|D|} \sum_{(x, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{y}) \in D} \sum_{j=1}^K w_{\Delta}(x, a_j) y_j$, where $w_{\Delta}(x, a_j) = \frac{\epsilon_R(x, a_j) - \epsilon_{R'}(x, a_j)}{\epsilon_0(x, a_j)}$.

modeling.label: Position-Specific Optimal Baselines for Delta-DCG
modeling.value: Variance-minimizing baselines for ranking, defined as $\beta^{\star}_{\perp \perp, j} = \frac{\text{E} \left[ w_{\Delta}(x, a_j)^2 y_j \right]}{\text{E} \left[ w_{\Delta}(x, a_j)^2 \right]}$ for each rank position $j$.

pipelineFlow: Interpret the randomized treatment assignment mechanism in A/B-testing as a meta-policy that defines a mixture over the treatment and control policies.
Apply $\Delta$-Off-Policy Estimation ($\Delta$-OPE) estimators, such as $\Delta$-IPS or $\Delta$-DR, to A/B-testing data logged under this meta-policy to obtain unbiased ATE estimates.
Leverage the resulting policy-aware importance weights $w_{\Delta}(x,a) = \frac{\Delta(a|x)}{\pi_0(a|x)}$ to exploit structural information about policy overlap, thereby reducing estimation noise.

For optimal treatment allocation, conduct a two-stage adaptive design: start with a balanced split, empirically estimate weighted residual variances, and then update the allocation ratio $p$ to minimize overall estimation variance.
For enhanced variance reduction, train reward models using the $\Delta$-MRDR objective, which selectively focuses model capacity on regions of policy disagreement.
Extend the framework to top-K ranking by employing the $\Delta$-DCG estimator and incorporating position-specific optimal baselines to mitigate variance explosion in combinatorial action spaces.
technicalDetails.reproducibility: The source code to reproduce all figures and numbers reported in the paper's Section 4 is available at github.com/olivierjeunen/delta-OPE-ABTesting/.

thesis: By reframing the randomized treatment assignment in A/B-testing as a meta-policy and leveraging $\Delta$-Off-Policy Estimation, a novel experimental protocol can exploit policy overlap to obtain unbiased, variance-reduced estimates for Average Treatment Effects, thereby accelerating experimentation and enhancing statistical power.
